personae.name: GHOST
personae.blurb: of the late king, Hamlet’s father

personae.name: GERTRUDE
personae.blurb: the Queen, Hamlet’s mother, now wife of Claudius

scenes.setting: Elsinore. A platform before the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Francisco and Barnardo, two sentinels.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Who’s there?

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: Nay, answer me. Stand and unfold yourself.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Long live the King!

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: Barnardo?

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: He.

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: You come most carefully upon your hour.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: ’Tis now struck twelve. Get thee to bed, Francisco.

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: For this relief much thanks. ’Tis bitter cold,

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: And I am sick at heart.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Have you had quiet guard?

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: Not a mouse stirring.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Well, good night.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: If you do meet Horatio and Marcellus,

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: The rivals of my watch, bid them make haste.
Enter Horatio and Marcellus.

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: I think I hear them. Stand, ho! Who is there?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Friends to this ground.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: And liegemen to the Dane.

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: Give you good night.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: O, farewell, honest soldier, who hath reliev’d you?

lines.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines.text: Barnardo has my place. Give you good-night.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Holla, Barnardo!

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Say, what, is Horatio there?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: A piece of him.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Welcome, Horatio. Welcome, good Marcellus.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: What, has this thing appear’d again tonight?

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: I have seen nothing.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Horatio says ’tis but our fantasy,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: And will not let belief take hold of him

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Touching this dreaded sight, twice seen of us.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Therefore I have entreated him along

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: With us to watch the minutes of this night,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: That if again this apparition come

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: He may approve our eyes and speak to it.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Tush, tush, ’twill not appear.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Sit down awhile,

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: And let us once again assail your ears,

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: That are so fortified against our story,

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: What we two nights have seen.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Well, sit we down,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And let us hear Barnardo speak of this.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Last night of all,

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: When yond same star that’s westward from the pole,

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Had made his course t’illume that part of heaven

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Where now it burns, Marcellus and myself,

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: The bell then beating one—

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Peace, break thee off. Look where it comes again.
Enter Ghost.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: In the same figure, like the King that’s dead.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Thou art a scholar; speak to it, Horatio.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Looks it not like the King? Mark it, Horatio.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Most like. It harrows me with fear and wonder.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: It would be spoke to.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Question it, Horatio.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: What art thou that usurp’st this time of night,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Together with that fair and warlike form

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: In which the majesty of buried Denmark

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Did sometimes march? By heaven I charge thee speak.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: It is offended.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: See, it stalks away.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Stay! speak, speak! I charge thee speak!
[_Exit Ghost._]

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: ’Tis gone, and will not answer.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: How now, Horatio! You tremble and look pale.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Is not this something more than fantasy?

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: What think you on’t?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Before my God, I might not this believe

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Without the sensible and true avouch

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Of mine own eyes.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Is it not like the King?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: As thou art to thyself:

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Such was the very armour he had on

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: When he th’ambitious Norway combated;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: So frown’d he once, when in an angry parle

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: He smote the sledded Polacks on the ice.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: ’Tis strange.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Thus twice before, and jump at this dead hour,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: With martial stalk hath he gone by our watch.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: In what particular thought to work I know not;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: But in the gross and scope of my opinion,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: This bodes some strange eruption to our state.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Good now, sit down, and tell me, he that knows,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Why this same strict and most observant watch

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: So nightly toils the subject of the land,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: And why such daily cast of brazen cannon

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: And foreign mart for implements of war;

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Why such impress of shipwrights, whose sore task

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Does not divide the Sunday from the week.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: What might be toward, that this sweaty haste

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Doth make the night joint-labourer with the day:

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Who is’t that can inform me?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: That can I;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: At least, the whisper goes so. Our last King,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Whose image even but now appear’d to us,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Was, as you know, by Fortinbras of Norway,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Thereto prick’d on by a most emulate pride,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Dar’d to the combat; in which our valiant Hamlet,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: For so this side of our known world esteem’d him,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Did slay this Fortinbras; who by a seal’d compact,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Well ratified by law and heraldry,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Did forfeit, with his life, all those his lands

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Which he stood seiz’d of, to the conqueror;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Against the which, a moiety competent

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Was gaged by our King; which had return’d

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: To the inheritance of Fortinbras,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Had he been vanquisher; as by the same cov’nant

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And carriage of the article design’d,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: His fell to Hamlet. Now, sir, young Fortinbras,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Of unimproved mettle, hot and full,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Hath in the skirts of Norway, here and there,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Shark’d up a list of lawless resolutes,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: For food and diet, to some enterprise

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: That hath a stomach in’t; which is no other,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: As it doth well appear unto our state,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: But to recover of us by strong hand

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And terms compulsatory, those foresaid lands

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: So by his father lost. And this, I take it,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Is the main motive of our preparations,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: The source of this our watch, and the chief head

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Of this post-haste and rummage in the land.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: I think it be no other but e’en so:

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Well may it sort that this portentous figure

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: Comes armed through our watch so like the King

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: That was and is the question of these wars.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: A mote it is to trouble the mind’s eye.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: In the most high and palmy state of Rome,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: A little ere the mightiest Julius fell,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: The graves stood tenantless and the sheeted dead

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Did squeak and gibber in the Roman streets;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: As stars with trains of fire and dews of blood,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Disasters in the sun; and the moist star,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Upon whose influence Neptune’s empire stands,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Was sick almost to doomsday with eclipse.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And even the like precurse of fierce events,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: As harbingers preceding still the fates

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And prologue to the omen coming on,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Have heaven and earth together demonstrated

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Unto our climatures and countrymen.
Re-enter Ghost.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: But, soft, behold! Lo, where it comes again!

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: I’ll cross it, though it blast me. Stay, illusion!

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: If thou hast any sound, or use of voice,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Speak to me.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: If there be any good thing to be done,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: That may to thee do ease, and grace to me,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Speak to me.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: If thou art privy to thy country’s fate,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Which, happily, foreknowing may avoid,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: O speak!

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Or if thou hast uphoarded in thy life

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Extorted treasure in the womb of earth,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: For which, they say, you spirits oft walk in death,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Speak of it. Stay, and speak!
[_The cock crows._]

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Stop it, Marcellus!

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Shall I strike at it with my partisan?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Do, if it will not stand.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: ’Tis here!

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: ’Tis here!
[_Exit Ghost._]

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: ’Tis gone!

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: We do it wrong, being so majestical,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: To offer it the show of violence,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: For it is as the air, invulnerable,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: And our vain blows malicious mockery.

lines.speaker: BARNARDO
lines.text: It was about to speak, when the cock crew.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And then it started, like a guilty thing

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Upon a fearful summons. I have heard

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: The cock, that is the trumpet to the morn,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Doth with his lofty and shrill-sounding throat

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Awake the god of day; and at his warning,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Whether in sea or fire, in earth or air,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Th’extravagant and erring spirit hies

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: To his confine. And of the truth herein

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: This present object made probation.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: It faded on the crowing of the cock.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Some say that ever ’gainst that season comes

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Wherein our Saviour’s birth is celebrated,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: The bird of dawning singeth all night long;

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: And then, they say, no spirit dare stir abroad,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: The nights are wholesome, then no planets strike,

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: No fairy takes, nor witch hath power to charm;

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: So hallow’d and so gracious is the time.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: So have I heard, and do in part believe it.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: But look, the morn in russet mantle clad,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Walks o’er the dew of yon high eastward hill.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Break we our watch up, and by my advice,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Let us impart what we have seen tonight

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Unto young Hamlet; for upon my life,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: This spirit, dumb to us, will speak to him.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Do you consent we shall acquaint him with it,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: As needful in our loves, fitting our duty?

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Let’s do’t, I pray, and I this morning know

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS
lines.text: Where we shall find him most conveniently.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Elsinore. A room of state in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Claudius King of Denmark, Gertrude the Queen, Hamlet, Polonius, Laertes, Voltemand, Cornelius, Lords and Attendant.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Though yet of Hamlet our dear brother’s death

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The memory be green, and that it us befitted

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To bear our hearts in grief, and our whole kingdom

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To be contracted in one brow of woe;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Yet so far hath discretion fought with nature

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That we with wisest sorrow think on him,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Together with remembrance of ourselves.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Therefore our sometime sister, now our queen,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Th’imperial jointress to this warlike state,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Have we, as ’twere with a defeated joy,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With one auspicious and one dropping eye,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With mirth in funeral, and with dirge in marriage,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In equal scale weighing delight and dole,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Taken to wife; nor have we herein barr’d

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Your better wisdoms, which have freely gone

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With this affair along. For all, our thanks.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Now follows, that you know young Fortinbras,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Holding a weak supposal of our worth,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Or thinking by our late dear brother’s death

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our state to be disjoint and out of frame,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Colleagued with this dream of his advantage,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He hath not fail’d to pester us with message,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Importing the surrender of those lands

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Lost by his father, with all bonds of law,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To our most valiant brother. So much for him.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Now for ourself and for this time of meeting:

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thus much the business is: we have here writ

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To Norway, uncle of young Fortinbras,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Who, impotent and bed-rid, scarcely hears

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of this his nephew’s purpose, to suppress

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: His further gait herein; in that the levies,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The lists, and full proportions are all made

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Out of his subject: and we here dispatch

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You, good Cornelius, and you, Voltemand,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For bearers of this greeting to old Norway,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Giving to you no further personal power

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To business with the King, more than the scope

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of these dilated articles allow.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Farewell; and let your haste commend your duty.

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS and VOLTEMAND
lines.text: In that, and all things, will we show our duty.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We doubt it nothing: heartily farewell.
[_Exeunt Voltemand and Cornelius._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And now, Laertes, what’s the news with you?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You told us of some suit. What is’t, Laertes?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You cannot speak of reason to the Dane,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And lose your voice. What wouldst thou beg, Laertes,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That shall not be my offer, not thy asking?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The head is not more native to the heart,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The hand more instrumental to the mouth,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Than is the throne of Denmark to thy father.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What wouldst thou have, Laertes?

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Dread my lord,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Your leave and favour to return to France,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: From whence though willingly I came to Denmark

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: To show my duty in your coronation;

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Yet now I must confess, that duty done,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: My thoughts and wishes bend again toward France,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: And bow them to your gracious leave and pardon.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Have you your father’s leave? What says Polonius?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: He hath, my lord, wrung from me my slow leave

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: By laboursome petition; and at last

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Upon his will I seal’d my hard consent.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I do beseech you give him leave to go.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Take thy fair hour, Laertes; time be thine,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And thy best graces spend it at thy will!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But now, my cousin Hamlet, and my son—
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: A little more than kin, and less than kind.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How is it that the clouds still hang on you?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Not so, my lord, I am too much i’ the sun.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Good Hamlet, cast thy nighted colour off,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And let thine eye look like a friend on Denmark.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Do not for ever with thy vailed lids

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Seek for thy noble father in the dust.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Thou know’st ’tis common, all that lives must die,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Passing through nature to eternity.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Ay, madam, it is common.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: If it be,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Why seems it so particular with thee?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Seems, madam! Nay, it is; I know not seems.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: ’Tis not alone my inky cloak, good mother,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Nor customary suits of solemn black,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Nor windy suspiration of forc’d breath,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: No, nor the fruitful river in the eye,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Nor the dejected haviour of the visage,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Together with all forms, moods, shows of grief,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: That can denote me truly. These indeed seem,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: For they are actions that a man might play;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: But I have that within which passeth show;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: These but the trappings and the suits of woe.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: ’Tis sweet and commendable in your nature, Hamlet,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To give these mourning duties to your father;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But you must know, your father lost a father,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That father lost, lost his, and the survivor bound

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In filial obligation, for some term

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To do obsequious sorrow. But to persevere

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In obstinate condolement is a course

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of impious stubbornness. ’Tis unmanly grief,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: It shows a will most incorrect to heaven,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A heart unfortified, a mind impatient,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: An understanding simple and unschool’d;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For what we know must be, and is as common

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As any the most vulgar thing to sense,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Why should we in our peevish opposition

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Take it to heart? Fie, ’tis a fault to heaven,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A fault against the dead, a fault to nature,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To reason most absurd, whose common theme

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is death of fathers, and who still hath cried,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: From the first corse till he that died today,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: ‘This must be so.’ We pray you throw to earth

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This unprevailing woe, and think of us

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As of a father; for let the world take note

lines.text: My father’s brother; but no more like my father

lines.text: Than I to Hercules. Within a month,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Ere yet the salt of most unrighteous tears

lines.text: Had left the flushing in her galled eyes,

lines.text: She married. O most wicked speed, to post

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: With such dexterity to incestuous sheets!

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: It is not, nor it cannot come to good.

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: To make it truster of your own report

lines.speaker: HORATIO

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Thrift, thrift, Horatio! The funeral bak’d meats

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Would I had met my dearest foe in heaven

lines.text: He was a man, take him for all in all,

lines.text: My lord, I think I saw him yesternight.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Saw? Who?

lines.speaker: HORATIO

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: The King my father!

lines.text: Season your admiration for a while

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: With an attent ear, till I may deliver

lines.speaker: HORATIO

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: This marvel to you.

lines.text: Marcellus and Barnardo, on their watch

lines.speaker: HORATIO

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Been thus encounter’d. A figure like your father,

lines.text: Armed at point exactly, cap-à-pie,

lines.text: Appears before them, and with solemn march

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Goes slow and stately by them: thrice he walk’d

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: By their oppress’d and fear-surprised eyes,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Within his truncheon’s length; whilst they, distill’d

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Almost to jelly with the act of fear,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Stand dumb, and speak not to him. This to me

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: In dreadful secrecy impart they did,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And I with them the third night kept the watch,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Where, as they had deliver’d, both in time,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Form of the thing, each word made true and good,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: The apparition comes. I knew your father;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: These hands are not more like.

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.text: My lord, upon the platform where we watch.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Did you not speak to it?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: My lord, I did;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: But answer made it none: yet once methought

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: It lifted up it head, and did address

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Itself to motion, like as it would speak.

lines.text: But even then the morning cock crew loud,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And at the sound it shrunk in haste away,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And vanish’d from our sight.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: ’Tis very strange.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: As I do live, my honour’d lord, ’tis true;

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: And we did think it writ down in our duty

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: To let you know of it.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Indeed, indeed, sirs, but this troubles me.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Hold you the watch tonight?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Arm’d, say you?

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: Arm’d, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: From top to toe?

lines.text: Then saw you not his face?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: What, look’d he frowningly?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: A countenance more in sorrow than in anger.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Pale, or red?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Nay, very pale.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And fix’d his eyes upon you?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Most constantly.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I would I had been there.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: It would have much amaz’d you.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Very like, very like. Stay’d it long?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: While one with moderate haste might tell a hundred.

lines.speaker: MARCELLUS and BARNARDO
lines.text: Longer, longer.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Not when I saw’t.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: His beard was grizzled, no?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: It was, as I have seen it in his life,

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: A sable silver’d.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I will watch tonight;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Perchance ’twill walk again.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: I warrant you it will.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: If it assume my noble father’s person,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I’ll speak to it, though hell itself should gape

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And bid me hold my peace. I pray you all,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: If you have hitherto conceal’d this sight,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Let it be tenable in your silence still;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And whatsoever else shall hap tonight,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Give it an understanding, but no tongue.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I will requite your loves. So, fare ye well.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Upon the platform ’twixt eleven and twelve,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I’ll visit you.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Our duty to your honour.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Your loves, as mine to you: farewell.
[_Exeunt Horatio, Marcellus and Barnardo._]

lines.text: The perfume and suppliance of a minute;

lines.text: Grows wide withal. Perhaps he loves you now,

lines.text: The virtue of his will; but you must fear,

lines.text: Carve for himself; for on his choice depends

lines.text: The sanctity and health of this whole state;

lines.text: If with too credent ear you list his songs,

lines.speaker: LAERTES

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: And keep you in the rear of your affection,

lines.speaker: LAERTES

lines.speaker: LAERTES

lines.speaker: LAERTES

lines.speaker: HAMLET

[_Exeunt._]
Enter Polonius and Reynaldo.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: REYNALDO
lines.text: My lord, I did intend it.

lines.text: Marry, well said; very well said. Look you, sir,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And how, and who, what means, and where they keep,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What company, at what expense; and finding

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: By this encompassment and drift of question,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That they do know my son, come you more nearer

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Than your particular demands will touch it.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Take you as ’twere some distant knowledge of him,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And in part him’—do you mark this, Reynaldo?

lines.speaker: REYNALDO
lines.text: Ay, very well, my lord.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: But, sir, such wanton, wild, and usual slips

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: REYNALDO
lines.text: My lord, that would dishonour him.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Faith no, as you may season it in the charge.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: You must not put another scandal on him,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That he is open to incontinency;

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That’s not my meaning: but breathe his faults so quaintly

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That they may seem the taints of liberty;

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: The flash and outbreak of a fiery mind,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: A savageness in unreclaimed blood,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Of general assault.

lines.speaker: REYNALDO
lines.text: But my good lord—

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Wherefore should you do this?

lines.speaker: REYNALDO
lines.text: Ay, my lord, I would know that.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Marry, sir, here’s my drift,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And I believe it is a fetch of warrant.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: You laying these slight sullies on my son,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: As ’twere a thing a little soil’d i’ th’ working,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Mark you,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Your party in converse, him you would sound,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Having ever seen in the prenominate crimes

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: The youth you breathe of guilty, be assur’d

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: ‘Good sir,’ or so; or ‘friend,’ or ‘gentleman’—

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: According to the phrase or the addition

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Of man and country.

lines.speaker: REYNALDO
lines.text: Very good, my lord.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And then, sir, does he this,—

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: He does—What was I about to say?

lines.text: At ‘closes in the consequence’ ay, marry!

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: God b’ wi’ you, fare you well.

lines.text: Observe his inclination in yourself.

[_Exit Reynaldo._]
Enter Ophelia.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: How now, Ophelia, what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: Alas, my lord, I have been so affrighted.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: With what, in the name of God?

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: My lord, as I was sewing in my chamber,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: Lord Hamlet, with his doublet all unbrac’d,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: No hat upon his head, his stockings foul’d,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: Ungart’red, and down-gyved to his ankle,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: Pale as his shirt, his knees knocking each other,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: And with a look so piteous in purport

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: As if he had been loosed out of hell

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: To speak of horrors, he comes before me.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Mad for thy love?

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: My lord, I do not know, but truly I do fear it.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What said he?

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: He took me by the wrist and held me hard;

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: Then goes he to the length of all his arm;

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: And with his other hand thus o’er his brow,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: He falls to such perusal of my face

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: As he would draw it. Long stay’d he so,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: At last,—a little shaking of mine arm,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: And thrice his head thus waving up and down,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: He rais’d a sigh so piteous and profound

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: As it did seem to shatter all his bulk

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: And end his being. That done, he lets me go,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: And with his head over his shoulder turn’d

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: He seem’d to find his way without his eyes,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: For out o’ doors he went without their help,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: And to the last bended their light on me.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Come, go with me. I will go seek the King.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: This is the very ecstasy of love,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Whose violent property fordoes itself,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And leads the will to desperate undertakings,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: As oft as any passion under heaven

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That does afflict our natures. I am sorry,—

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What, have you given him any hard words of late?

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: No, my good lord; but as you did command,

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: I did repel his letters and denied

lines.speaker: OPHELIA
lines.text: His access to me.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That hath made him mad.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I am sorry that with better heed and judgement

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I had not quoted him. I fear’d he did but trifle,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And meant to wreck thee. But beshrew my jealousy!

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: It seems it is as proper to our age

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: To cast beyond ourselves in our opinions

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: As it is common for the younger sort

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: To lack discretion. Come, go we to the King.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: This must be known, which, being kept close, might move

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: More grief to hide than hate to utter love.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter King, Queen, Rosencrantz, Guildenstern and Attendants.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Welcome, dear Rosencrantz and Guildenstern.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Moreover that we much did long to see you,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The need we have to use you did provoke

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our hasty sending. Something have you heard

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of Hamlet’s transformation; so I call it,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Since nor th’exterior nor the inward man

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Resembles that it was. What it should be,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: More than his father’s death, that thus hath put him

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So much from th’understanding of himself,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I cannot dream of. I entreat you both

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That, being of so young days brought up with him,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And since so neighbour’d to his youth and humour,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That you vouchsafe your rest here in our court

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Some little time, so by your companies

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To draw him on to pleasures and to gather,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So much as from occasion you may glean,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Whether aught to us unknown afflicts him thus

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That, open’d, lies within our remedy.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Good gentlemen, he hath much talk’d of you,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And sure I am, two men there are not living

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To whom he more adheres. If it will please you

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To show us so much gentry and good will

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: As to expend your time with us awhile,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: For the supply and profit of our hope,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Your visitation shall receive such thanks

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: As fits a king’s remembrance.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Both your majesties

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Might, by the sovereign power you have of us,

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Put your dread pleasures more into command

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Than to entreaty.

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: We both obey,

lines.text: And here give up ourselves, in the full bent,

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thanks, Rosencrantz and gentle Guildenstern.

lines.text: Thanks, Guildenstern and gentle Rosencrantz.

lines.text: And I beseech you instantly to visit

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: My too much changed son. Go, some of you,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And bring these gentlemen where Hamlet is.

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: Heavens make our presence and our practices

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: Pleasant and helpful to him.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Ay, amen.
[_Exeunt Rosencrantz, Guildenstern and some Attendants._]
Enter Polonius.

lines.text: Th’ambassadors from Norway, my good lord,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Are joyfully return’d.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou still hast been the father of good news.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Have I, my lord? Assure you, my good liege,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I hold my duty, as I hold my soul,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Both to my God and to my gracious King:

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And I do think,—or else this brain of mine

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Hunts not the trail of policy so sure

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: As it hath us’d to do—that I have found

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: The very cause of Hamlet’s lunacy.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: O speak of that, that do I long to hear.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Give first admittance to th’ambassadors;

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: My news shall be the fruit to that great feast.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thyself do grace to them, and bring them in.
[_Exit Polonius._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He tells me, my sweet queen, that he hath found

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The head and source of all your son’s distemper.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I doubt it is no other but the main,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: His father’s death and our o’erhasty marriage.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Well, we shall sift him.
Enter Polonius with Voltemand and Cornelius.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Welcome, my good friends!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Say, Voltemand, what from our brother Norway?

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: Most fair return of greetings and desires.

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: Upon our first, he sent out to suppress

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: His nephew’s levies, which to him appear’d

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: To be a preparation ’gainst the Polack;

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: But better look’d into, he truly found

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: It was against your Highness; whereat griev’d,

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: That so his sickness, age, and impotence

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: Was falsely borne in hand, sends out arrests

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: On Fortinbras; which he, in brief, obeys,

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: Receives rebuke from Norway; and in fine,

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: Makes vow before his uncle never more

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: Whereon old Norway, overcome with joy,

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: And his commission to employ those soldiers

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: So levied as before, against the Polack:

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: With an entreaty, herein further shown,
[_Gives a paper._]

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: That it might please you to give quiet pass

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND
lines.text: Through your dominions for this enterprise,

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND

lines.speaker: VOLTEMAND

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: It likes us well;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And at our more consider’d time we’ll read,

lines.speaker: KING

[_Exeunt Voltemand and Cornelius._]

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: This business is well ended.

lines.text: My liege and madam, to expostulate

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What majesty should be, what duty is,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Why day is day, night night, and time is time

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Were nothing but to waste night, day and time.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Therefore, since brevity is the soul of wit,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And tediousness the limbs and outward flourishes,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I will be brief. Your noble son is mad.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Mad call I it; for to define true madness,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What is’t but to be nothing else but mad?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.text: More matter, with less art.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That he is mad, ’tis true: ’tis true ’tis pity;

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And pity ’tis ’tis true. A foolish figure,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: But farewell it, for I will use no art.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Mad let us grant him then. And now remains

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That we find out the cause of this effect,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: _these; in her excellent white bosom, these, &c._

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Came this from Hamlet to her?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Good madam, stay awhile; I will be faithful.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: _Doubt thou the stars are fire,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Doubt that the sun doth move,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Doubt truth to be a liar,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: O dear Ophelia, I am ill at these numbers. I have not art to reckon my

lines.text: groans. But that I love thee best, O most best, believe it. Adieu.

lines.text: But how hath she receiv’d his love?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What do you think of me?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As of a man faithful and honourable.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I would fain prove so. But what might you think,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: When I had seen this hot love on the wing,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: As I perceiv’d it, I must tell you that,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Before my daughter told me, what might you,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Or my dear Majesty your queen here, think,

lines.text: If I had play’d the desk or table-book,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Or given my heart a winking, mute and dumb,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.speaker: POLONIUS

lines.text: It may be, very likely.

lines.text: When it prov’d otherwise?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Not that I know.

lines.text: Take this from this, if this be otherwise.

lines.text: Where truth is hid, though it were hid indeed

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Within the centre.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How may we try it further?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: You know sometimes he walks four hours together

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Here in the lobby.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: So he does indeed.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: At such a time I’ll loose my daughter to him.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Be you and I behind an arras then,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Mark the encounter. If he love her not,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: And be not from his reason fall’n thereon,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Let me be no assistant for a state,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: But keep a farm and carters.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We will try it.
Enter Hamlet, reading.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: But look where sadly the poor wretch comes reading.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Away, I do beseech you, both away

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I’ll board him presently. O, give me leave.
[_Exeunt King, Queen and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: How does my good Lord Hamlet?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Well, God-a-mercy.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Do you know me, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Excellent well. You are a fishmonger.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Not I, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Then I would you were so honest a man.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Honest, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Ay sir, to be honest, as this world goes, is to be one man picked out

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: of ten thousand.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: That’s very true, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: For if the sun breed maggots in a dead dog, being a good kissing

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: carrion,—

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Have you a daughter?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I have, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Let her not walk i’ th’ sun. Conception is a blessing, but not as your

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: daughter may conceive. Friend, look to’t.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: How say you by that? [_Aside._] Still harping on my daughter. Yet he

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: knew me not at first; he said I was a fishmonger. He is far gone, far

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: gone. And truly in my youth I suffered much extremity for love; very

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: near this. I’ll speak to him again.—What do you read, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Words, words, words.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What is the matter, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Between who?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: I mean the matter that you read, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Slanders, sir. For the satirical slave says here that old men have grey

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: beards; that their faces are wrinkled; their eyes purging thick amber

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: and plum-tree gum; and that they have a plentiful lack of wit, together

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: with most weak hams. All which, sir, though I most powerfully and

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: potently believe, yet I hold it not honesty to have it thus set down.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: For you yourself, sir, should be old as I am, if like a crab you could

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: go backward.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Though this be madness, yet there is method in’t.—

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Will you walk out of the air, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Into my grave?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Indeed, that is out o’ the air. [_Aside._] How pregnant sometimes his

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: replies are! A happiness that often madness hits on, which reason and

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: sanity could not so prosperously be delivered of. I will leave him and

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: suddenly contrive the means of meeting between him and my daughter.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: My honourable lord, I will most humbly take my leave of you.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: You cannot, sir, take from me anything that I will more willingly part

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: withal, except my life, except my life, except my life.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Fare you well, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: These tedious old fools.
Enter Rosencrantz and Guildenstern.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: You go to seek the Lord Hamlet; there he is.
[_To Polonius._]

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: God save you, sir.
[_Exit Polonius._]

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: My honoured lord!

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: My most dear lord!

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: My excellent good friends! How dost thou, Guildenstern? Ah,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Rosencrantz. Good lads, how do ye both?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: As the indifferent children of the earth.

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: Happy in that we are not over-happy;

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: On Fortune’s cap we are not the very button.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Nor the soles of her shoe?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Neither, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Then you live about her waist, or in the middle of her favours?

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: Faith, her privates we.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: In the secret parts of Fortune? O, most true; she is a strumpet. What’s

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: the news?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: None, my lord, but that the world’s grown honest.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Then is doomsday near. But your news is not true. Let me question more

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: in particular. What have you, my good friends, deserved at the hands of

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Fortune, that she sends you to prison hither?

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: Prison, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Denmark’s a prison.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Then is the world one.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: A goodly one; in which there are many confines, wards, and dungeons,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Denmark being one o’ th’ worst.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: We think not so, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why, then ’tis none to you; for there is nothing either good or bad but

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: thinking makes it so. To me it is a prison.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Why, then your ambition makes it one; ’tis too narrow for your mind.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: O God, I could be bounded in a nutshell, and count myself a king of

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: infinite space, were it not that I have bad dreams.

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: Which dreams, indeed, are ambition; for the very substance of the

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: ambitious is merely the shadow of a dream.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: A dream itself is but a shadow.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Truly, and I hold ambition of so airy and light a quality that it is

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: but a shadow’s shadow.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Then are our beggars bodies, and our monarchs and outstretch’d heroes

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: the beggars’ shadows. Shall we to th’ court? For, by my fay, I cannot

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: reason.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: We’ll wait upon you.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: No such matter. I will not sort you with the rest of my servants; for,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: to speak to you like an honest man, I am most dreadfully attended. But,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: in the beaten way of friendship, what make you at Elsinore?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: To visit you, my lord, no other occasion.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Beggar that I am, I am even poor in thanks; but I thank you. And sure,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: dear friends, my thanks are too dear a halfpenny. Were you not sent

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: for? Is it your own inclining? Is it a free visitation? Come, deal

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: justly with me. Come, come; nay, speak.

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: What should we say, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why, anything. But to the purpose. You were sent for; and there is a

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: kind of confession in your looks, which your modesties have not craft

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: enough to colour. I know the good King and Queen have sent for you.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: To what end, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: That you must teach me. But let me conjure you, by the rights of our

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: fellowship, by the consonancy of our youth, by the obligation of our

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: ever-preserved love, and by what more dear a better proposer could

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: charge you withal, be even and direct with me, whether you were sent

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: for or no.
[_To Guildenstern._]

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: What say you?
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Nay, then I have an eye of you. If you love me, hold not

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: off.

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: My lord, we were sent for.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I will tell you why; so shall my anticipation prevent your discovery,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: and your secrecy to the King and Queen moult no feather. I have of

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: late, but wherefore I know not, lost all my mirth, forgone all custom

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: of exercises; and indeed, it goes so heavily with my disposition that

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: this goodly frame the earth, seems to me a sterile promontory; this

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: most excellent canopy the air, look you, this brave o’erhanging

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: firmament, this majestical roof fretted with golden fire, why, it

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: appears no other thing to me than a foul and pestilent congregation of

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: vapours. What a piece of work is man, how noble in reason, how infinite

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: in faculties, in form and moving, how express and admirable; in action

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: how like an angel, in apprehension, how like a god: the beauty of the

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: world, the paragon of animals. And yet, to me, what is this

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: quintessence of dust? Man delights not me; no, nor woman neither,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: though by your smiling you seem to say so.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: My lord, there was no such stuff in my thoughts.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why did you laugh then, when I said ‘Man delights not me’?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: To think, my lord, if you delight not in man, what Lenten entertainment

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: the players shall receive from you. We coted them on the way, and

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: hither are they coming to offer you service.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: He that plays the king shall be welcome,—his Majesty shall have tribute

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: of me; the adventurous knight shall use his foil and target; the lover

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: shall not sigh gratis, the humorous man shall end his part in peace;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: the clown shall make those laugh whose lungs are tickle o’ th’ sere;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: and the lady shall say her mind freely, or the blank verse shall halt

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: for’t. What players are they?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Even those you were wont to take such delight in—the tragedians of the

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: city.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How chances it they travel? Their residence, both in reputation and

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: profit, was better both ways.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: I think their inhibition comes by the means of the late innovation.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Do they hold the same estimation they did when I was in the city? Are

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: they so followed?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: No, indeed, they are not.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How comes it? Do they grow rusty?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Nay, their endeavour keeps in the wonted pace; but there is, sir, an

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: aerie of children, little eyases, that cry out on the top of question,

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: and are most tyrannically clapped for’t. These are now the fashion, and

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: so berattle the common stages—so they call them—that many wearing

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: rapiers are afraid of goose-quills and dare scarce come thither.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: What, are they children? Who maintains ’em? How are they escoted? Will

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: they pursue the quality no longer than they can sing? Will they not say

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: afterwards, if they should grow themselves to common players—as it is

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: most like, if their means are no better—their writers do them wrong to

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: make them exclaim against their own succession?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Faith, there has been much to do on both sides; and the nation holds it

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: no sin to tarre them to controversy. There was for a while, no money

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: bid for argument unless the poet and the player went to cuffs in the

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: question.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Is’t possible?

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: O, there has been much throwing about of brains.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Do the boys carry it away?

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Ay, that they do, my lord. Hercules and his load too.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: It is not very strange; for my uncle is King of Denmark, and those that

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: would make mouths at him while my father lived, give twenty, forty,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: fifty, a hundred ducats apiece for his picture in little. ’Sblood,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: there is something in this more than natural, if philosophy could find

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: it out.
[_Flourish of trumpets within._]

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: There are the players.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Gentlemen, you are welcome to Elsinore. Your hands, come. The

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: appurtenance of welcome is fashion and ceremony. Let me comply with you

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: in this garb, lest my extent to the players, which I tell you must show

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: fairly outward, should more appear like entertainment than yours. You

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: are welcome. But my uncle-father and aunt-mother are deceived.

lines.speaker: GUILDENSTERN
lines.text: In what, my dear lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I am but mad north-north-west. When the wind is southerly, I know a

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: hawk from a handsaw.
Enter Polonius.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Well be with you, gentlemen.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Hark you, Guildenstern, and you too, at each ear a hearer. That great

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: baby you see there is not yet out of his swaddling clouts.

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: Happily he’s the second time come to them; for they say an old man is

lines.speaker: ROSENCRANTZ
lines.text: twice a child.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I will prophesy he comes to tell me of the players. Mark it.—You say

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: right, sir: for a Monday morning ’twas so indeed.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: My lord, I have news to tell you.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: My lord, I have news to tell you. When Roscius was an actor in Rome—

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: The actors are come hither, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Buzz, buzz.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Upon my honour.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Then came each actor on his ass—

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: The best actors in the world, either for tragedy, comedy, history,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: pastoral, pastoral-comical, historical-pastoral, tragical-historical,

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: tragical-comical-historical-pastoral, scene individable, or poem

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: unlimited. Seneca cannot be too heavy, nor Plautus too light, for the

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: law of writ and the liberty. These are the only men.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: O Jephthah, judge of Israel, what a treasure hadst thou!

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What treasure had he, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why—

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: ’One fair daughter, and no more,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: The which he loved passing well.’
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: Still on my daughter.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Am I not i’ th’ right, old Jephthah?

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: If you call me Jephthah, my lord, I have a daughter that I love passing

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: well.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Nay, that follows not.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: What follows then, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: As by lot, God wot,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: and then, you know,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: It came to pass, as most like it was.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: The first row of the pious chanson will show you more. For look where

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: my abridgement comes.
Enter four or five Players.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: You are welcome, masters, welcome all. I am glad to see thee well.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Welcome, good friends. O, my old friend! Thy face is valanc’d since I

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: saw thee last. Com’st thou to beard me in Denmark? What, my young lady

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: and mistress! By’r lady, your ladyship is nearer to heaven than when I

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: saw you last, by the altitude of a chopine. Pray God your voice, like a

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: piece of uncurrent gold, be not cracked within the ring. Masters, you

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: are all welcome. We’ll e’en to’t like French falconers, fly at anything

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: we see. We’ll have a speech straight. Come, give us a taste of your

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: quality. Come, a passionate speech.

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: What speech, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I heard thee speak me a speech once, but it was never acted, or if it

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: was, not above once, for the play, I remember, pleased not the million,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: ’twas caviare to the general. But it was—as I received it, and others,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: whose judgements in such matters cried in the top of mine—an excellent

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: play, well digested in the scenes, set down with as much modesty as

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: cunning. I remember one said there were no sallets in the lines to make

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: the matter savoury, nor no matter in the phrase that might indite the

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: author of affectation, but called it an honest method, as wholesome as

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: sweet, and by very much more handsome than fine. One speech in it, I

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: chiefly loved. ’Twas Aeneas’ tale to Dido, and thereabout of it

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: especially where he speaks of Priam’s slaughter. If it live in your

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: memory, begin at this line, let me see, let me see:

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: _The rugged Pyrrhus, like th’ Hyrcanian beast,—_

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: It is not so: it begins with Pyrrhus—

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: _The rugged Pyrrhus, he whose sable arms,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Black as his purpose, did the night resemble

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: When he lay couched in the ominous horse,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Hath now this dread and black complexion smear’d

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: With heraldry more dismal. Head to foot

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Now is he total gules, horridly trick’d

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: With blood of fathers, mothers, daughters, sons,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Bak’d and impasted with the parching streets,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: That lend a tyrannous and a damned light

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: To their vile murders. Roasted in wrath and fire,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And thus o’ersized with coagulate gore,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: With eyes like carbuncles, the hellish Pyrrhus

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Old grandsire Priam seeks._

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: So, proceed you.

lines.speaker: POLONIUS
lines.text: ’Fore God, my lord, well spoken, with good accent and good discretion.

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: _Anon he finds him,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Striking too short at Greeks. His antique sword,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Rebellious to his arm, lies where it falls,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Repugnant to command. Unequal match’d,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Pyrrhus at Priam drives, in rage strikes wide;

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: But with the whiff and wind of his fell sword

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Th’unnerved father falls. Then senseless Ilium,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Seeming to feel this blow, with flaming top

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Stoops to his base, and with a hideous crash

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Takes prisoner Pyrrhus’ ear. For lo, his sword,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Which was declining on the milky head

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Of reverend Priam, seem’d i’ th’air to stick.

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: So, as a painted tyrant, Pyrrhus stood,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: And like a neutral to his will and matter,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: Did nothing.

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: But as we often see against some storm,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: A silence in the heavens, the rack stand still,

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
lines.text: The bold winds speechless, and the orb below

lines.speaker: FIRST PLAYER
