lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Who is to be buried in’t?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: One that was a woman, sir; but, rest her soul, she’s dead.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How absolute the knave is! We must speak by the card, or equivocation

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: will undo us. By the Lord, Horatio, these three years I have taken note

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: of it, the age is grown so picked that the toe of the peasant comes so

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: near the heel of the courtier he galls his kibe.—How long hast thou

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: been a grave-maker?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Of all the days i’ th’ year, I came to’t that day that our last King

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Hamlet o’ercame Fortinbras.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How long is that since?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Cannot you tell that? Every fool can tell that. It was the very day

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: that young Hamlet was born,—he that is mad, and sent into England.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Ay, marry, why was he sent into England?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Why, because he was mad; he shall recover his wits there; or if he do

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: not, it’s no great matter there.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: ’Twill not be seen in him there; there the men are as mad as he.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How came he mad?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Very strangely, they say.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How strangely?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Faith, e’en with losing his wits.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Upon what ground?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Why, here in Denmark. I have been sexton here, man and boy, thirty

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: years.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How long will a man lie i’ th’earth ere he rot?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Faith, if he be not rotten before he die,—as we have many pocky corses

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: nowadays that will scarce hold the laying in,—he will last you some

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: eight year or nine year. A tanner will last you nine year.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why he more than another?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: Why, sir, his hide is so tann’d with his trade that he will keep out

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: water a great while. And your water is a sore decayer of your whoreson

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: dead body. Here’s a skull now; this skull hath lain in the earth

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: three-and-twenty years.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Whose was it?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: A whoreson, mad fellow’s it was. Whose do you think it was?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Nay, I know not.

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: A pestilence on him for a mad rogue! A pour’d a flagon of Rhenish on my

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: head once. This same skull, sir, was Yorick’s skull, the King’s jester.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: This?

lines.speaker: FIRST CLOWN
lines.text: E’en that.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Let me see. [_Takes the skull._] Alas, poor Yorick. I knew him,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Horatio, a fellow of infinite jest, of most excellent fancy. He hath

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: borne me on his back a thousand times; and now, how abhorred in my

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: imagination it is! My gorge rises at it. Here hung those lips that I

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: have kiss’d I know not how oft. Where be your gibes now? your gambols?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: your songs? your flashes of merriment, that were wont to set the table

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: on a roar? Not one now, to mock your own grinning? Quite chop-fallen?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Now get you to my lady’s chamber, and tell her, let her paint an inch

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: thick, to this favour she must come. Make her laugh at that.—Prithee,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Horatio, tell me one thing.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: What’s that, my lord?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Dost thou think Alexander looked o’ this fashion i’ th’earth?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: E’en so.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And smelt so? Pah!
[_Throws down the skull._]

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: E’en so, my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: To what base uses we may return, Horatio! Why may not imagination trace

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: the noble dust of Alexander till he find it stopping a bung-hole?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: ’Twere to consider too curiously to consider so.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: No, faith, not a jot. But to follow him thither with modesty enough,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: and likelihood to lead it; as thus. Alexander died, Alexander was

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: buried, Alexander returneth into dust; the dust is earth; of earth we

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: make loam; and why of that loam whereto he was converted might they not

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: stop a beer-barrel?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Imperious Caesar, dead and turn’d to clay,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Might stop a hole to keep the wind away.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: O, that that earth which kept the world in awe

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Should patch a wall t’expel the winter’s flaw.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: But soft! but soft! aside! Here comes the King.
Enter priests, &c, in procession; the corpse of Ophelia, Laertes and Mourners following; King, Queen, their Trains, &c.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: The Queen, the courtiers. Who is that they follow?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And with such maimed rites? This doth betoken

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: The corse they follow did with desperate hand

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Fordo it own life. ’Twas of some estate.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Couch we awhile and mark.
[_Retiring with Horatio._]

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: What ceremony else?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: That is Laertes, a very noble youth. Mark.

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: What ceremony else?

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Her obsequies have been as far enlarg’d

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: As we have warranties. Her death was doubtful;

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: And but that great command o’ersways the order,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: She should in ground unsanctified have lodg’d

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Till the last trumpet. For charitable prayers,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Shards, flints, and pebbles should be thrown on her.

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Yet here she is allowed her virgin rites,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Her maiden strewments, and the bringing home

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Of bell and burial.

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Must there no more be done?

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: No more be done.

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: We should profane the service of the dead

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: To sing sage requiem and such rest to her

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: As to peace-parted souls.

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Lay her i’ th’earth,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: And from her fair and unpolluted flesh

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: May violets spring. I tell thee, churlish priest,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: A minist’ring angel shall my sister be

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: When thou liest howling.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: What, the fair Ophelia?
[_Scattering flowers._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Sweets to the sweet. Farewell.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I hop’d thou shouldst have been my Hamlet’s wife;

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I thought thy bride-bed to have deck’d, sweet maid,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And not have strew’d thy grave.

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: O, treble woe

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Fall ten times treble on that cursed head

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Whose wicked deed thy most ingenious sense

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Depriv’d thee of. Hold off the earth a while,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Till I have caught her once more in mine arms.
[_Leaps into the grave._]

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Now pile your dust upon the quick and dead,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Till of this flat a mountain you have made,

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: To o’ertop old Pelion or the skyish head

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: Of blue Olympus.
[_Advancing._]

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: What is he whose grief

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Bears such an emphasis? whose phrase of sorrow

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Conjures the wand’ring stars, and makes them stand

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Like wonder-wounded hearers? This is I,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Hamlet the Dane.
[_Leaps into the grave._]
[_Grappling with him._]

lines.speaker: LAERTES
lines.text: The devil take thy soul!

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Thou pray’st not well.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I prithee take thy fingers from my throat;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: For though I am not splenative and rash,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Yet have I in me something dangerous,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Which let thy wiseness fear. Away thy hand!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Pluck them asunder.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Hamlet! Hamlet!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Gentlemen!

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Good my lord, be quiet.
[_The Attendants part them, and they come out of the grave._]

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why, I will fight with him upon this theme

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Until my eyelids will no longer wag.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: O my son, what theme?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I lov’d Ophelia; forty thousand brothers

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Could not, with all their quantity of love,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Make up my sum. What wilt thou do for her?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: O, he is mad, Laertes.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: For love of God forbear him!

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: ’Swounds, show me what thou’lt do:

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Woul’t weep? woul’t fight? woul’t fast? woul’t tear thyself?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Woul’t drink up eisel? eat a crocodile?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I’ll do’t. Dost thou come here to whine?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: To outface me with leaping in her grave?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Be buried quick with her, and so will I.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And if thou prate of mountains, let them throw

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Millions of acres on us, till our ground,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Singeing his pate against the burning zone,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Make Ossa like a wart. Nay, an thou’lt mouth,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I’ll rant as well as thou.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: This is mere madness:

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And thus awhile the fit will work on him;

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Anon, as patient as the female dove,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: When that her golden couplets are disclos’d,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: His silence will sit drooping.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Hear you, sir;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: What is the reason that you use me thus?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I lov’d you ever. But it is no matter.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Let Hercules himself do what he may,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: The cat will mew, and dog will have his day.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I pray thee, good Horatio, wait upon him.
[_Exit Horatio._]
[_To Laertes_]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Strengthen your patience in our last night’s speech;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We’ll put the matter to the present push.—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Good Gertrude, set some watch over your son.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This grave shall have a living monument.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: An hour of quiet shortly shall we see;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Till then in patience our proceeding be.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Hamlet and Horatio.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: So much for this, sir. Now let me see the other;

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: You do remember all the circumstance?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Remember it, my lord!

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Sir, in my heart there was a kind of fighting

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: That would not let me sleep. Methought I lay

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Worse than the mutinies in the bilboes. Rashly,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And prais’d be rashness for it,—let us know,

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: When our deep plots do pall; and that should teach us

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: There’s a divinity that shapes our ends,

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: That is most certain.

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.text: My sea-gown scarf’d about me, in the dark

lines.text: Grop’d I to find out them; had my desire,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Finger’d their packet, and in fine, withdrew

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: To mine own room again, making so bold,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: My fears forgetting manners, to unseal

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Their grand commission; where I found, Horatio,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Oh royal knavery! an exact command,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Larded with many several sorts of reasons,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Importing Denmark’s health, and England’s too,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: With ho! such bugs and goblins in my life,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: That on the supervise, no leisure bated,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: No, not to stay the grinding of the axe,

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.text: Is’t possible?

lines.text: But wilt thou hear me how I did proceed?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: I beseech you.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Being thus benetted round with villanies,—

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Or I could make a prologue to my brains,

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Devis’d a new commission, wrote it fair:

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I once did hold it, as our statists do,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: A baseness to write fair, and labour’d much

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: How to forget that learning; but, sir, now

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: It did me yeoman’s service. Wilt thou know

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: The effect of what I wrote?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Ay, good my lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: An earnest conjuration from the King,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: As England was his faithful tributary,

lines.text: As love between them like the palm might flourish,

lines.text: As peace should still her wheaten garland wear

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And stand a comma ’tween their amities,

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.text: He should the bearers put to sudden death,

lines.text: Not shriving-time allow’d.

lines.text: How was this seal’d?

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why, even in that was heaven ordinant.

lines.text: I had my father’s signet in my purse,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Which was the model of that Danish seal:

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Folded the writ up in the form of the other,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Subscrib’d it: gave’t th’impression; plac’d it safely,

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.text: Was our sea-fight, and what to this was sequent

lines.text: Thou know’st already.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: So Guildenstern and Rosencrantz go to’t.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Why, man, they did make love to this employment.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: They are not near my conscience; their defeat

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Does by their own insinuation grow.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: ’Tis dangerous when the baser nature comes

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Between the pass and fell incensed points

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Of mighty opposites.

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: Why, what a king is this!

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Does it not, thinks’t thee, stand me now upon,—

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: He that hath kill’d my king, and whor’d my mother,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Popp’d in between th’election and my hopes,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Thrown out his angle for my proper life,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And with such cozenage—is’t not perfect conscience

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: What is the issue of the business there.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: And a man’s life’s no more than to say ‘One’.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: But I am very sorry, good Horatio,

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: For by the image of my cause I see

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: But sure the bravery of his grief did put me

Enter Osric.

lines.speaker: OSRIC
lines.text: Your lordship is right welcome back to Denmark.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: I humbly thank you, sir. Dost know this waterfly?

lines.speaker: HORATIO
lines.text: No, my good lord.

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: Thy state is the more gracious; for ’tis a vice to know him. He hath

lines.text: much land, and fertile; let a beast be lord of beasts, and his crib

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: shall stand at the king’s mess; ’tis a chough; but, as I say, spacious

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.text: to you from his Majesty.

lines.speaker: HAMLET

lines.speaker: HAMLET
lines.text: right use; ’tis for the head.

lines.speaker: OSRIC
lines.text: I thank your lordship, ’tis very hot.

lines.text: No, believe me, ’tis very cold, the wind is northerly.

lines.speaker: OSRIC
lines.text: It is indifferent cold, my lord, indeed.

lines.speaker: OSRIC

lines.text: I know you are not ignorant,—
